scope: First-party review of 15 tools across customer service, translation, scientific research, enterprise search, inference infrastructure, legal work, RAG and vector databases, model routing, music, video and ML operations.

accepted.name: Decagon
accepted.userValue: Decagon builds customer-facing AI agents that can handle real service tasks such as membership changes and bookings, rather than only answering FAQ-style questions.

accepted.name: DeepL
accepted.userValue: DeepL combines translation, document workflows, real-time voice translation, writing refinement and developer APIs, with glossaries and style controls for consistent multilingual work.

accepted.name: Elicit
accepted.userValue: Elicit searches academic papers and creates structured, cited research reports; its current Research Agent combines paper discovery, extraction and paper-specific Q&A, while systematic-review workflows provide guided screening and PRISMA-style reporting.

accepted.name: Glean
accepted.userValue: Glean connects workplace apps and documents, returns permission-aware answers with citations, helps draft work and lets teams build and govern agents that execute tasks across systems.

accepted.name: Groq
accepted.userValue: Groq provides a developer inference API with OpenAI-compatible endpoints and an inference-focused cloud built around its LPU architecture and GPU infrastructure.

accepted.name: Harvey
accepted.userValue: Harvey provides purpose-built legal agents, secure document workspaces, legal and regulatory research, contract intelligence and collaboration controls for professional legal work.

accepted.name: LlamaIndex
accepted.userValue: LlamaIndex combines an open-source framework for agents and retrieval-augmented generation with managed LlamaParse for parsing, extracting, classifying and indexing complex documents.

accepted.name: OpenRouter
accepted.userValue: OpenRouter exposes many models and providers through one compatible API, with automatic fallback, typed SDKs, an agent SDK, local developer tools and MCP access.

accepted.name: Pinecone
accepted.userValue: Pinecone provides managed vector indexes and retrieval infrastructure for RAG and AI agents, with tools for managing indexes, querying vectors and grounding agent knowledge.

accepted.name: Poe
accepted.userValue: Poe provides a multi-model chat interface and a creator platform for prompt bots, server bots, script bots, API bots and interactive Canvas apps, including monetization options.

accepted.name: Replicate
accepted.userValue: Replicate lets developers run public models through a browser playground or API, fine-tune models on their data and deploy custom models; its maintained official models have stable APIs and predictable pricing.

accepted.name: Suno
accepted.userValue: Suno generates songs from prompts and audio inputs, supports remixing, editing, stem separation and custom models; its official plans distinguish personal free use from paid commercial-use rights.

accepted.name: Synthesia
accepted.userValue: Synthesia creates business videos from scripts, PowerPoint files, documents, links or prompts with AI avatars, voices, translation, dubbing and interactive video features.

accepted.name: Together AI
accepted.userValue: Together AI combines serverless and dedicated inference, custom model training and GPU compute in one AI-native cloud platform for production applications.

accepted.name: Weights & Biases
accepted.userValue: Weights & Biases combines experiment tracking and model workflows with Weave tracing and evaluation for AI applications, plus serverless training and inference products.
